title: How to Convert Your Cyber Security Salary Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a cyber security salary hourly rate to annual pay using 38-hour weeks, plus tax, super, and casual loading explained with Fair Work figures.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay equals the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, a $50 per hour cyber security role gives $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 gross per year. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. The calculator on this site uses 38 hours by default, but you can change it to match your actual hours.

faqs.q: What is the difference between minimum wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 per hour for casuals including 25% loading). Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations. For example, cyber security roles may be covered by the Professional Employees Award or an industry-specific award. Award rates include classifications with higher pay for skills and experience. Always check the relevant Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide for your award. Many cyber security salaries are above award, but the minimum legal pay is the award rate.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). On this site, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator applies it automatically. The loading increases your gross pay, but remember that super is calculated on your ordinary earnings, which includes the loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion for Cyber Security Salaries

Whether you're negotiating a cyber security salary or comparing job offers, converting an hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard week under many awards and the National Employment Standards), the multiplier is 1,976 hours (38 × 52). This gives you the gross annual figure before tax, super, and other deductions.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Ombudsman defines full-time hours as 38 per week for most awards. Some roles may have different ordinary hours, but 38 is the default assumption on this site. If your cyber security role specifies 40 hours, simply use 40 in the calculation. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you adjust the weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, a $60 per hour cyber security analyst working 38 hours earns $2,280 per week, so $4,560 per fortnight. This is useful for budgeting and comparing with advertised salaries.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Cyber Security Salaries

It's important to distinguish between the legal minimum and what you might actually earn in cyber security.

### National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates apply to employees not covered by an award or agreement. See [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) for the latest figures.

### Award Rates

Most cyber security roles fall under awards such as the Professional Employees Award or the Clerks Award, depending on duties. Award rates are higher than the minimum wage and include classification levels based on skills and experience. For example, a Level 1 IT professional under the Professional Employees Award has a minimum hourly rate above $30. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, which list the exact rates and allowances.

### Above-Award Salaries

Many cyber security salaries are negotiated well above award rates. According to industry surveys, entry-level cyber security analysts might earn $70,000–$90,000 per year, while senior roles can exceed $150,000. The calculator on this site works for any hourly rate you enter, whether it's award-based or market-driven.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. On this site, check the casual loading box and enter your base hourly rate (without loading). The calculator will add 25% automatically. For more detail, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Super Guarantee

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual gross pay is $100,000, your employer must contribute an additional $12,000 into your super fund. The super amount is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra cost for the employer. The calculator estimates super on your ordinary earnings only, and stops at the cap.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates.

### Tax Brackets 2026–27

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

These are marginal rates, meaning each portion of your income is taxed at the corresponding rate. The Medicare levy of 2% applies to most residents, with reductions for low-income earners. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

### Example: Cyber Security Salary of $100,000

For a gross annual salary of $100,000 (e.g., $50.51 per hour for 38 hours):
- Tax: approximately $22,967 (including Medicare)
- Net pay: around $77,033 per year, or $1,481 per week

This is an estimate. Your actual tax may differ if you have HELP debt, salary packaging, or other factors.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay on this site is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise figures, use the [reference tables](/data) on this site or consult a tax professional. Always check the relevant Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide for your award to ensure you're receiving at least the minimum entitlements.
